rules.text: Keep one consistent visual style across a batch (same theme colours, same font, same layout profile). Don't change style mid-batch without a reason.
rules.author: director

rules.text: Speaker first. Don't force something into every moment -- many stretches should be just the speaker + captions.
rules.author: director

rules.text: On-screen text repeats what the speaker is saying at that moment: short, one idea at a time.
rules.author: director

rules.text: No complicated worked examples or mock UIs invented for the clip. They make people read and confuse the topic.
rules.author: director

rules.text: Never invent content -- no made-up end cards, steps or claims. Everything on screen comes from the recording.
rules.author: director

rules.text: Cut filler phrases and dead pauses where there is a clean gap; never clip a word in half.
rules.author: director

rules.text: Images/pop-ins are welcome when literal to the words being said. Brief full-screen moments may hide the speaker for a beat.
rules.author: director

rules.text: Don't be afraid of duration -- be afraid of unnecessary or boring parts. Add context that makes a point land, even if it makes the clip longer.
rules.author: director

rules.text: Title on screen from frame 0 when the clip needs framing to be understood cold.
rules.author: director

rules.text: Subtle SFX only (whoosh, pop, soft click, typing), well under the voice. Sound off by default until the user supplies SFX files.
rules.author: director

rules.text: Give numbers and references their context (a bare year or stat needs a one-line label). Drop lines a viewer can't parse rather than leaving them unclear.
rules.author: director

rules.text: The opening must be paid off inside the clip -- never open on a question only answered outside it. Cut repetition: when the speaker says the same point twice, keep one version.
rules.author: director

rules.text: When teaching from a live screen share, keep the screen recording visible for the whole relevant stretch, zoomed to what is being discussed so it reads on a phone. Keep the speaker visible too (a smaller card is fine).
rules.author: director
